newsitem.title: USA: Option Care outlines growth strategy.
newsitem.headline: Option Care outlines growth strategy.

text.p: Option Care Inc, a provider of home health care, said it expects to expand its regional clusters by acquiring franchises and independent operators in 1997.

"Through this strategy we expect to achieve top-line growth of 25 percent to 30 percent, with net income tracking in the four percent to six percent (range) over the next several years," said president Erick Hanson.
Hanson noted that during 1996 the company either closed or sold seven underperforming offices, a move he expects will have a positive impact on 1997 results.

Earlier, the company posted a fourth-quarter loss of $23 million or $2.18 per share, which included a $24.2 million writeoff of goodwill, most of which relates to the 1991 purchase of Option Care from its predecessor, Sutter Home Care.
Excluding the charge, quarterly earnings were $0.08 per share compared with $0.05 a year earlier. Option Care said the writeoff should be accretive to earnings in 1997.
"Although a writeoff is undesirable, it is evidence of the successful implementation of our growth strategy," Hanson said in a statement.
